answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat trust as a graph, not a headcount. Each identity is a vertex whose edges are earned through completed, verifiable work for others, not self-declared claims. A newcomer starts as a willow shoot: flexible but weak, able to take only tiny jobs until its vertex accumulates real endorsements. No haven exists for fake identities, because reputation cannot be transferred or bought in bulk; cloning an identity copies no edges. An attacker must therefore pay the full cost of doing genuine work for every fake vertex, while honest agents pay it only once.
